title: Akshaye Khanna Makes Telugu Debut as Shukracharya in Mythological Epic Mahakali
excerpt: Riding the wave of his career-defining turn in Dhurandhar, Bollywood actor Akshaye Khanna steps into Prasanth Varma's cinematic universe with a dramatically transformed mythological avatar that has already drawn comparisons to Amitabh Bachchan.
body:
• Akshaye Khanna will play Asuraguru Shukracharya in Mahakali, part of the Prasanth Varma Cinematic Universe (PVCU) that began with HanuMan (2024).
  • The film marks Khanna's debut in Telugu cinema. It is directed by Puja Aparna Kolluru and produced by RKD Studios.
  • Khanna has completed filming his portions. The film will release in multiple languages including Hindi, capitalizing on his post-Dhurandhar popularity.
  • Bhoomi Shetty plays the lead role of Maha, making her the first female superhero in the PVCU.

Akshaye Khanna, whose career has experienced a dramatic resurgence over the past year, is stepping into unfamiliar territory — and an entirely new language. The Bollywood actor will make his Telugu cinema debut in Mahakali, an upcoming mythological superhero film from the Prasanth Varma Cinematic Universe (PVCU), playing the role of Asuraguru Shukracharya.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=qsltjDNCkxA

Director Prasanth Varma announced the casting on X with a first-look poster that immediately set social media buzzing. "In the shadows of gods, rose the brightest flame of rebellion. Presenting The Enigmatic Akshaye Khanna as the eternal 'Asuraguru SHUKRACHARYA' from Mahakali," Varma wrote.

A Dramatic Transformation

The poster shows Khanna completely unrecognizable. He appears in menacing form with flowing silver hair pulled into a top bun, his eyes glinting in darkness — a far cry from the suave, suited characters that defined his earlier career. The look drew immediate comparisons to Amitabh Bachchan's Ashwatthama in Nag Ashwin's Telugu epic Kalki 2898AD, though Khanna's Shukracharya occupies a different mythological space.

In Hindu mythology, Shukracharya is the guru of the Asuras (demons), a figure of immense knowledge and strategic cunning who serves as a counterpoint to the Devas' guru, Brihaspati. Varma's version appears to reimagine the character within the PVCU's superhero framework, positioning Shukracharya as a complex antagonist rather than a straightforward villain.

"We had signed Akshaye Sir much before Dhurandhar. He is the highlight of Mahakali."

— Prasanth Varma, Creator and Co-Writer, PVCU

Riding the Dhurandhar Wave

Khanna's casting in Mahakali predates his recent box-office triumphs, but the timing could not be better. His portrayal of Rahman Dakait in Aditya Dhar's Dhurandhar (2025), opposite Ranveer Singh, became a cultural moment. Social media was flooded with fans celebrating his effortless menace and screen presence. His role as Aurangzeb in Laxman Utekar's Chhaava (2025) further cemented his resurgence.

The twin successes prompted a significant career recalibration. Reports emerged that Khanna revised his fee to Rs 21 crore, leading to his exit from Drishyam 3 over remuneration and creative disagreements. Jaideep Ahlawat replaced him in that franchise.

The Dhurandhar wave has also reshaped Mahakali's release strategy. Originally planned as a Telugu-only release, the film will now have a Hindi version to capitalize on Khanna's newfound pan-India appeal. "After Dhurandhar, there will be a Hindi version highlighting Akshaye Khanna in the marketing," Varma confirmed.

Inside the PVCU

Mahakali is a key installment in the Prasanth Varma Cinematic Universe, the shared franchise that launched with the surprise hit HanuMan in 2024. The universe draws from Hindu mythology to build an interconnected superhero narrative — a concept that has found resonance with Indian audiences hungry for homegrown genre cinema.

The film is directed by Puja Aparna Kolluru and produced by RKD Studios, with Varma serving as creator and co-writer. Music is by Smaran Sai, with cinematography by Suresh Ragutu. Actress Bhoomi Shetty plays the lead role of Maha, making her the first female superhero in the PVCU.

Khanna reportedly completed filming his portions by March 2026, with the production team still needing around 40 days of additional shooting in Hyderabad for the remaining cast. A release date has not been announced, but the film is expected later this year or in early 2027.

What It Means for Cross-Industry Casting

Khanna's Telugu debut reflects a broader trend in Indian cinema: the erosion of language barriers between film industries. Post-pandemic hits like RRR, Pushpa, and KGF demonstrated that audiences across India are open to films regardless of their language of origin. Dhurandhar's success, which made Khanna a viral sensation beyond traditional Bollywood circles, made the Mahakali crossover a natural fit.

For Indian-American audiences who have followed Khanna since his 1997 debut in Border and through films like Dil Chahta Hai and Race, this new phase is a welcome vindication. Khanna spent years choosing selective projects with mixed commercial results. The current streak — villain roles with genuine menace and star power — has made him one of Indian cinema's most compelling performers at 51.

Varma, who visited the sets to celebrate Khanna's birthday during filming, left no doubt about what the collaboration means: "A true actor who proves that real talent doesn't need noise. Effortless screen presence, powerful performances, and unmatched class always stand out."
